steps.title: my, your, his, her, our, their
steps.html:
PersonPossessiveExample
ImyThis is my brother.
youyourIs that your wife?
hehisHis parents are divorced.
sheherHer husband is Turkish.
weourOur children are twins.
theytheirTheir flat is small.

These words never change: his brother, his sister, his parents.

Use his for a man and her for a woman — not for the thing that follows.

Learners often write her husband is a doctor as she husband. After a possessive there is no is.

steps.title: Possessive 's and s'
steps.html:
FormExample
one personname + 'sThis is Zafar's wife.
one person ending in -sname + 'sJames's car
more than one personplural + s'my parents' house
irregular pluralplural + 'sthe children's room

's can also be the short form of is: Zafar's a doctor = Zafar is a doctor.

Look at what comes next. A noun after it (Zafar's wife) means it is a possessive.

steps.title: The royal family
steps.html:
Queen Elizabeth II was the queen of the United Kingdom for seventy years. Her husband was Prince Philip. Their oldest son is the king now – King Charles III.

Charles and his first wife, Diana, had two sons, William and Harry. Charles and Diana divorced in 1996. Today Charles's wife is Queen Camilla, so she is William's stepmother.

William is Charles's older son. His wife is Catherine. Their three children are George, Charlotte and Louis.

Harry is married to Meghan, and Harry and Meghan live in America now with their two children. Harry is George's uncle, so George is Harry's nephew, and Meghan is George's aunt. Harry's children are George's cousins.
